head.name: @fzlt/core/presence
head.lead: Lockstep input exchange for multiplayer, behind a tiny transport adapter. Every peer runs the same fixed-step simulation from the same seed. Each sim frame needs every player's input for that frame; your own input is sent delay frames ahead, so on a good link the game never waits. A missing input stalls the sim (never guesses), so peers can't drift apart. Inputs live in fixed rings of typed arrays: a confirmed per-frame input log a rollback layer can replay. State hashes are exchanged every hashEvery frames to catch a desync early.

items.doc: Wire kinds. Every message is 12 bytes: kind, slot, players, mode, u32 frame (or seed), u32 value (or token). From the room: WELCOME, LEAVE, RESUME (a seat is back: resend), AWAY (a seat dropped and may come back), LOBBY (before the start: your seat, room size, seated); START goes to the room from the host (the protocol: /guides/build-your-own-room-server/).

items.doc: Join a room (a server speaking the fizlet-rooms subprotocol): resolves when the room starts with your seat, the player count, the shared seed and the host's mode. protocols go to the WebSocket handshake: the room reads its access token there (["fizlet-rooms", "invite." + code]), so the code stays out of the URL and the logs. A dropped link (1006, or a server restart: 1011, 1012, 1014) reconnects on its own (o.retry) with the seat's resume token, kept in memory only (never in a URL); the room's own closes (idle, full, seat gone, the caps) end it.

items.name: @fzlt/core/presence/rollback
items.summary: Rollback netcode for a deterministic sim, on presence's 12-byte wire and room (nothing in the room server changes). Presence's lockstep waits for every input, so on a phone's network the sim runs only as fast as the slowest round trip; this runs every frame at once instead. Each frame runs with this screen's own input (a small delay, 1 to 3 frames, picked from the measured latency) and a guess for everyone else's (the last input heard from them). When a real input arrives that differs from the guess, the state goes back to that frame (a ring of snapshots of the sim's byte views, made once) and the frames since run again: the sim is deterministic, so every screen ends on the same state. A frame whose inputs are all real is final: confirm hears each one, in order, once; state hashes are compared on final frames only (a desync shows; it never drifts). A screen that runs ahead of the others (by the trip each side measures, carried in the INPUT message's spare byte) waits a frame now and then until they meet. At most window frames run past the last final one: past it the sim waits (a link that went quiet). A seat the room says left plays gone from the frame after its last input, on every screen. No allocation per frame. Wire: INPUT [1, seat, delay, lead × 2 (int8), frame u32, bits u32], HASH [2, seat, 0, 0, frame, hash]. One INPUT per frame, frames rising (the room relays each once; over TCP nothing is lost or reordered, and a resend only follows a RESUME).
